title: Save me from my religion. Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven. “So when you give to the needy, do not announce it with trumpets, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honoured by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your giving may be in secret. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by others. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But when you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father, who is unseen. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you. And when you pray, do not keep on babbling like pagans, for they think they will be heard because of their many words. Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him. “This, then, is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’ For if you forgive other people when they sin against you, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive others their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.“
devotional:
When you fast, do not look sombre as the hypocrites do, for they disfigure their faces to show others they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have received their reward in full. But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face, so that it will not be obvious to others that you are fasting, but only to your Father, who is unseen; and your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.’’

So why is focusing on the external, and seeking the approval of men such a threat to authentic spirituality?

When our focus is on how we look, and when the approval of others is essential for life, then we are driven by our insecurities. The Pharisees of Jesus’ day did their righteous acts before men, because they were basically very insecure. They wanted to be liked, they wanted to be thought highly of, they wanted to be looked upon with a sense of respect, they wanted to be considered to be spiritual and they wanted the seal of approval from others. So their whole life was about how others saw them. Why were they driven by insecurities?

When our focus is on how we look, and when the approval of others is essential for life, then we will never be able to be honest or real. So often how we look is so disconnected from how we are. We want to give the impression that we are strong, that we have got it all sorted, that we’re doing okay, but in reality we are feel far from God, we are plagued with doubts and confusion, and we would love someone to come along and put their arm round us and just accepts us in our mess. Being a follower of Jesus is a call to honesty and reality, not hypocrisy

“Hypocrisy,” Barclay explains is “the sin of using religion to cover up sin. A hypocrite is not a person who falls short of his high ideals, or who occasionally sins, because all of us experience these failures. A hypocrite deliberately uses religion to cover up his sins and promote his own gains.” thepreachersword.com

So to be a hypocrite is much more serious than an inconsistent life, it is the deliberate use of religious activity to deceive others and hide your own sin and failure and need in order to promote a false image about yourself, in order to get the approval of others.

When our focus is on how we look, and when the approval of others is essential for life, then we are judging spirituality wrongly. I find it very interesting how we conclude if a person is spiritual or not. The Pharisees believed that if a person kept all external rules, i.e. if they were seen to attend the place of worship, and practised spiritual disciplines then they must be spiritual people. In our day we have fallen into the same trap, we think if a person goes to church, reads their bible, has a quiet time, wears the right clothes, and reads a certain version of the bible then they must be okay spiritually. But that is like trying to use a speedometer to measure the weight of something. God evaluates our spiritual life’s not by what we do, but by who we are. By the condition of our hearts and what we carry in them. I have seen this so often, and I have been guilty of it too, where people use religious activity to hide what is really going on in our hearts.

When our focus is on how we look, and when the approval of others is essential for life, we end up with spiritual fatigue. Wearing a mask, pretending to be someone we are not is extremely hard work and saps our energy. Hiding behind a mask and refusing to be honest and real will never encourage or enrich a life. Rather it will drain a person of life and hope, and we won’t experience the love and acceptance we crave. Sadly, some Christians keep themselves so busy either trying to be noticed, or trying to ease the ache of the emptiness that they carry in their hearts.
prayer: Father I confess that hiding and pretending are exhausting. Help me to always be real and honest with you and with those around me.
